topics.label: Lecture framing and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture’s scope, connects it to previous lectures, and sets out the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Signaling mutations that deregulate growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways allow cancer cells to proliferate and survive without normal growth controls.

topics.label: Differentiation defects in blood cancers and intestinal epithelium
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cancer cell’s differentiation state shapes its abnormal proliferation and tissue appearance.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of the balance between pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic proteins allows cancer cells to evade death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and cancer cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits normal cell division and how increased telomerase expression enables cancer cells to bypass that limit.

topics.label: p53 safeguards and the growth-control hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain and consolidate how cellular safeguards oppose the loss of growth control caused by mutations and cellular stress.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and participates in self-reinforcing changes to gene regulation.

topics.label: The angiogenic switch in tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit a blood supply to overcome the limits imposed by oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic spread, survival and genetic characteristics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells reach distant sites and what determines whether they establish detectable metastases.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by restating its central takeaway, recommending further reading, and inviting questions.
